chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say regarding Al-Ila' (oath of abstention from wife): 'If a man makes an oath not to approach his wife, nor touch her, nor join his head with hers, he is in ease (has time) as long as four months do not pass. When the four months pass, he is stopped (held accountable). Either he returns (to intimacy) and touches her, or he resolves on divorce and releases her. Until she menstruates and purifies from her menses, he divorces her with one pronouncement before he has intercourse with her, with the testimony of two just witnesses. Then he is more entitled to take her back as long as the three menstrual periods (of waiting) do not pass.'

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةِ: The right of revocation/taking back the wife during the waiting period
key_terms.الْأَقْرَاءِ: Menstrual periods (used to measure the waiting period)
key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Oath of abstaining from sexual intercourse with one's wife

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure and timeline for Al-Ila' (oath of abstention) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* elaborates on the jurisprudence of Al-Ila', establishing a four-month grace period during which the husband may resume intimacy or commit to divorce. It specifies that the final divorce must occur after the wife’s menses and purification, prior to cohabitation, thereby preserving the husband's right to revocation (Raj'a) within the three menstrual cycles, a nuance critical to Shia legal theory regarding the timing of Talaq.
